messages:
maria_garcia: Heads-up — Acme production (dedicated pool eu-west-1-dedicated-3) started spiking p95 token latency and returning intermittent 429s around 03:15 UTC. Customer says it correlates to jobs pinned to 1g MIG slices on the same host. Samples attached below.

jonathan_kim: Do we have a sample request_id and the model + slice config?

maria_garcia: request_id=01H7ZQ2X-ACME-987, model=redwood-2-xl, slice=MIG 1g. Log snippet: 
```
2026-03-16T03:16:02Z request_id=01H7ZQ2X-ACME-987 model=redwood-2-xl slice=1g p95=1.2s status=200 tokens=512
2026-03-16T03:16:17Z request_id=01H7ZQ2X-ACME-988 model=redwood-2-xl slice=1g p95=3.8s status=429 tokens=512
2026-03-16T03:16:29Z request_id=01H7ZQ2X-ACME-989 model=redwood-2-xl slice=1g p95=0.9s status=200 tokens=512
```

sam_liu: First guess: co-located tenants using different MIG sizes can cause SM and L3 cache thrashing on shared host. Can you run the node-level util snapshot? I want SM%, L3 BW, mem BW, and NVSwitch/fabric.

maria_garcia: Pasted metrics snapshot from node n-42: 
```
SM_util=89%, L3_bw=92% (bursting), vram_util=78%, nvlink_bw=40GB/s, active_migs=[1g,1g,2g,3g]
```

anita_patel: Noted. Autoscaler didn't upscale? Our dedicated autoscale policy only looks at queue length of the routing frontends — it misses short, high-p95 bursts driven by single-tenant SM saturation. That explains why we saw throttles instead of node pool scale.

support_oncall: I'm going to try a repro: spin up a synthetic load targeting 1g slices on n-42 with same sequence length and concurrency. If we reproduce, we should test forcing coarser MIG partitioning (convert to all 2g or 3g) and see if L3 contention drops.

sam_liu: Repro command (internal test harness):
```
infra-load --target-node n-42 --model redwood-2-xl --slices 1g --concurrency 16 --seq 1024 --duration 600
```

infra-bot: Snapshot for n-42 (03:18 UTC): SM_util=94%, L3_bw=95%, p95_tokens=3.6s, drops=12/600 (2%).

maria_garcia: Confirmed — repro shows repeated p95 spikes and a small increase in 429s after ~80s of sustained load. Looks like thermal/SM backpressure or L3 eviction hotspots.

jonathan_kim: Two mitigation paths: 1) Quick — migrate ACME's dedicated workload to a different node pool with uniform MIG sizes (can be done via pool drain + redeploy). 2) Medium — adjust autoscale to consider GPU SM/L3 metrics and token latency signals. 3) Long — add per-tenant isolation heuristics so heavy KV-cache workloads get homogenous packing.

anita_patel: For immediate relief, I suggest a redeploy to a temporary pool with 2g slices only. Also open an autoscale ticket to change trigger conditions: add sm_util > 75% for >=120s or token_p95_breach count.

support_oncall: I'll perform hot-migrate to pool eu-west-1-dedicated-7 (2g slices) and monitor. ETA 10m.

maria_garcia: FYI customer is expecting a follow-up and possible credits — they saw production errors and billing confusion because retries were generating extra tokens. Please include billing in the postmortem.

sam_liu: After migration, record these traces: kernel latencies, L3 eviction rate, and kvcache miss rate. We need concrete before/after numbers to justify migration and design changes.

infra-bot: Migration started at 03:28 UTC (task id mig-6452).

support_oncall: Migration complete at 03:34 UTC. Early metrics: SM_util=46%, L3_bw=31%, p95_tokens=0.72s, 429_rate=0.1%.

maria_garcia: Looks much better. Customer notified. I've filed support ticket #SUP-1298 with action items: (a) recommend permanent pool with homogeneous MIG sizes, (b) autoscale metric change request, (c) billing review.

jonathan_kim: Thanks. Follow-up: lets run a controlled A/B test to quantify cost delta of 2g-only pool vs mixed packing for same throughput. If cost delta < 10% it's an easy recommendation.

anita_patel: Agreed. I'll create the autoscale RFC and add sm/L3 triggers.

support_oncall: Marking this thread resolved for now — will update SUP-1298 with postmortem once A/B results are in. :thumbsup:
